name: Fish Tacos with Avocado & Grapes (Two Ways)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe was created to feed two adults and two young children. You know your child (their tastes and appetite) best. Use this recipe as a template, adjusting ingredients, cooking methods, and portions as needed.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 lime
1 jalapeño pepper
227 g red grapes
½ small bunch cilantro

instructions.primary_message: Juice lime into a medium bowl. Add honey and spices, then whisk to combine the dressing.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 tsp honey
¼ tsp oregano, dried
¼ tsp salt
⅛ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon to reduce spice level, then small dice. Add to the bowl with the dressing. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Peel and mince garlic and shallot. Add both to the bowl.
Using a clean cutting board, cut half of the grapes into quarters, place on a plate, and set aside. Thinly slice remaining grapes, add to the bowl, stir to combine, and set aside.
Place oil and spices in a medium bowl, then stir to combine the spice paste.
instructions.secondary_message:
extra virgin olive oil
1 tsp chili powder
¼ tsp salt
⅛ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, pat tilapia dry with paper towels. Add to the bowl with the spice paste and turn to coat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add tilapia and cook until opaque and flaky, 3-4 minutes per side. Remove to another plate.

Meanwhile, halve and pit avocados; using a spoon, scoop out the flesh. Slice half of an avocado lengthwise into ½-inch thick wedges and add to the plate with the quartered grapes. Small dice remaining avocado, then add to the bowl with the sliced grapes. Set the plate aside.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl, stir to combine the salsa, and set aside.
Warm tortillas in another skillet, oven, or microwave (optional).
Use a fork to break the tilapia into bite-sized pieces.

FOR THE KID PLATES: Divide a ½-cup of tilapia, halved grapes, and avocado wedges between plates. Spread 2 tortillas with butter, roll tightly, cut in half, and divide between plates.

FOR THE ADULT PLATES: Divide remaining tortillas between plates, then fill with tilapia and salsa. Enjoy!
